Sustainable development requires direct actions where it is needed most. Geospatial information helps us identify those needed, measure change and make better decisions. Thank you, Mr Chair.
I thank the distinguished representative of Armenia. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Chile.

Thank you, Chair.

Chile takes note of the report and we value the work carried out by the working group on geospatial information and the secretariat to strengthen the role of geospatial information support of sustainable development. In line with our national experience, we highlight the importance of incorporating the geospatial dimension from the design of indicators and data production to promote effective interoperability across information systems across member states. Chile believes it is fundamental to set geospatial information as a strategic asset for public policy and decision-making, supporting the development of policy documents and other materials that will help to ensure its contribution to sustainable development. Similarly, we support the creation of a working team under the auspices of the Bureau of the Committee to strengthen their value proposal and use cases on priority issues. Finally, we also feel it is essential to strengthen collaboration between the and member states in the United Nations system and other relevant actors through coordination mechanisms, data exchange and capacity development supported by human and financial resources are sufficient to ensure results. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Chile. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Cuba.

Thank you very much, co-chair. Cuba is fully committed to achieving Agenda 2030 and the SDGs. In this regard, geospatial information is meaningful and significant insofar as it provides data and statistics that are relevant in the area of looking after the environment, agriculture, land use planning, and natural resources. In this regard, to guarantee the provision of data, we're working on modernizing our national network, together with seismic and marine centres. In this way, we are helping to contribute to the prevention of natural disasters. However, this important work has been hampered as a result of the energy blockade and other unilateral coercive measures and the blockade of the United States against our country. This limits access to advanced technologies, specialised equipment, software and international financing, all of this makes the modernization of our geospatial infrastructure more difficult and more expensive and it prevents our efforts at sustainable development. in this context, there have been blockages to our geospatial information systems that require fuel and many other things. All of this has led to delays in programs aimed at implementing the integrated framework in Cuba. Work on controls of geospatial information, topographic research, cadastral research, population and housing censuses have all been delayed. This increases the digital gap and makes it difficult for Cuba to contribute to geospatial management and geospatial information management systems. Thank you very much.
I thank the distinguished representative of Cuba. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Jamaica.

Thank you, Mr. Chair. Jamaica thanks the Secretariat and the Working Group on Geospatial Information of the Interagency and Expert Group on SDG Indicators for their report and supports a renewed implementation focused approach to geospatial information for sustainable development. As a small island developing state, Jamaica considers location-based information essential for identifying development gaps, targeting limited resources and protecting development gains from climate related shocks. Jamaica continues to integrate the SDGs through Vision 2030 Jamaica, but our 2026 Voluntary National Review confirms that important data gaps remain. which underscores the need to bring statistical and geospatial information together earlier in the data production process and to improve timely, geographically disaggregated information since national averages can conceal significant differences amongst parishes, communities, and urban and rural areas. Jamaica encourages stronger engagement with the private sector, academia and civil society and supports a renewed approach that strengthens national ownership and preserves a strong focus on capacity development for small island developing states consistent with the Antigua and Barbuda agenda. Thank you, Mr. Chair.
I thank the distinguished representative of Jamaica. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Belgium.

Mr. President.

The Kingdom of Belgium supports the proposal aimed at strengthening the role of geospatial information over the course of the last years of the 2030 Agenda and the post 2030 programme. The high level forum yesterday showed that what we do in our committee addresses real urgent needs, but that more accessible and repeated communications on this are necessary. Geospatial information should be better recognized from the outset as a crucial component of the development implementation follow up and assessment of policies. We thus favor the idea of the Bureau advancing this work and presenting a renewed approach to the committee at its 17th session. This should lead to a clear value proposal with concrete examples at a national level with a limited list of use cases on the priority theme of sustainable development. We encourage the Bureau to look to support from the working group on existing geospatial information and also to look to the expertise available within the regional committees and other existing bodies. If a specific task team is created, their mandate should be targeted and limited in time and their coordination with the existing working group should be clearly defined in order to avoid duplication or work on parallel tracks. Finally, the policy we've mentioned in the report should be easily accessible, if possible in several languages, in order to then be reused by member states and the regional committees in turn. I thank you, Chair.
